data.title: Format of applications
data.text:
An application to a single appeal judge or a panel of the Court of Appeal must be in Form AP-3 and must (a) state briefly the grounds for filing the application, (b) identify the material or evidence intended to be relied on, (c) refer precisely to any applicable provision of an enactment or rule, and (d) state the remedy sought.

data.title: Format of memorandum
data.text:

rules.text:

commentary.text:
“Rule 14.57 provides that ‘A party or person may be added, removed or substituted as a party to an appeal in accordance with rule 3.74’. Rule 3.74(3) directs the Court’s attention to the requirement that adding a party should not cause ‘prejudice . . . that could not be remedied by a costs award, an adjournment or the imposition of terms’”. Walton Development and Management Inc. v. Osman Auction Inc., [2015] A.J. No. 1010, 2015 ABCA 298 at para. 11 (Alta. C.A.).
An applicant seeking to be added as a party to an appeal must first establish a legal interest in the outcome of the proceedings. Once that is shown, the court must consider: (1) whether it is just and convenient to add the applicant; and (2) whether the applicant’s interest can be adequately protected only if it is granted party status. Ravvin v. Canada Bread Co., [2020] A.J. No. 817, 2020 ABCA 287 at paras. 4 and 7 (Alta. C.A.); Town of Canmore v. Three Sisters Mountain Village Properties Ltd., [2022] A.J. No. 1003, 2022 ABCA

(1) No later than 10 days before an appeal is scheduled to be heard, a party may serve on the party to whom the offer is made a formal offer to settle the appeal or any part of the appeal in accordance with Part 4 , Division 5 .

commentary.text:
The result of reading rule 14.59(1) and Part 4, Division 5 together is that rule 14.59(1) is not restricted to appeals and may also include applications. Morin v. Alberta (Utilities Commission), [2017] A.J. No. 87, 2017 ABCA 39 at para. 10 (Alta. C.A.). Together, these rules can play a role in managing litigation at the appeal level, if a party brings an application that is without merit, a respondent should be entitled to avail itself of the compromise rule in an effort to dissuade the applicant from continuing with its application. Morin v. Alberta (Utilities Commission), [2017] A.J. No. 87, 2017 ABCA 39 at para. 10 (Alta. C.A.).
An offer to settle must be one that is reasonable and realistic. The court’s assessment of this entails a consideration of an examination of all of the surrounding circumstances existing at the time the offer was served and remained open, as well as the outcome of the appeal. Baim v. North Country Catering Ltd., [2017] A.J. No. 1047, 2017 ABCA 332 at para. 10 (Alta. C.A.), citing , [2006] A.J. No. 377, 2006 ABCA 101 at paras. 14-17 Allen (Next Friend of) v. Mueller (Alta. C.A.). The “offer to settle must include an element of compromise in order to be seen to be genuine”. Baim v. North Country Catering Ltd., [2017] A.J. No. 1047, 2017 ABCA 332 at para. 10 (Alta. C.A.).
For example, an offer to forego appeal costs if the appeal is discontinued or an offer to pay $1.00 would be and, therefore, inadequate; but an offer to forego a previous costs de minimus award, agree to settle part of outstanding litigation or discount an extent judgment would be sufficient compromises. H2S Solutions Ltd. v. Tourmaline Oil Corp., [2020] A.J. No. 575, 2020 ABCA 201 at para. 34 (Alta. C.A.).

rules.title: Suspension of time periods
rules.text:
(1) Once a date has been scheduled for judicial dispute resolution, time limits in respect of the appeal are suspended until an order or direction is made under subrule (2).
(2) If judicial dispute resolution is not successful, (a) the appeal judge conducting the judicial dispute resolution will set time limits for filing and serving any remaining materials on the appeal, or (b) if no order is made under clause (a) a case management officer may provide a direction setting the time limits for filing and serving any remaining materials on the appeal.

rules.title: Failure to meet deadlines
rules.text:
An appeal must be struck by the Registrar if (a) the appellant has failed to file the Appeal Record within the time period set out in these rules, (b) the appellant has failed to file its factum (i) before the expiry of the deadline for filing the factum in a standard appeal set out in rule 14.23(1) [Filing factums – standard appeals], or (ii) by the deadline for filing the factum in a fast track appeal set out in rule 14.24(1)(a) , [Filing factums – fast track appeals]
(c) a standard appeal has not been placed on the Civil Appeal Hearing List before the earlier of (i) 6 months after the deadline for the filing of the last factum in the appeal, and (ii) 12 months after the filing of the notice of appeal, or R. 14.63 [Alta. Rule 14.64 provides that the Registrar must strike an appeal if:
• the appellant fails to file the Appeal Record within four months from the date on which the appellant filed the notice of appeal for standard appeals (rules 14.16(3) and 14.64(a)), or not later than one month from the date on which the notice of appeal was filed for fast track appeals (rules 4.17(1) and 14.64(a)); For standard appeals. See, for example: Barry v. Institute of Chartered Accountants of Alberta, Complaints Inquiry Committee MacLeod , [2016] A.J. No. 308, 2016 ABCA 89 at para. 19 (Alta. C.A.); v. Alberta College of Social Workers, [2017] A.J. No. 19, 2017 ABCA 11 at para. 1 (Alta. C.A.); for fast track appeals, see, for example: , [2016] A.J. No. 210, 2016 ABCA 62 at para. 2 (Alta. Bacon v. Gullberg C.A.).
• the appellant fails to file a factum on time (rules 14.23(1), 14.64(b));
• the standard appeal is not placed on the Civil Appeal Hearing List within stipulated periods (rule 14.64(c)); Coleman v. Coleman, [2014] A.J. No. 1443, 2014 ABCA 452 at para. 21, footnote 4 (Alta. rules.title: Restoring appeals
rules.text:
(1) An appeal or application for permission to appeal that has been struck by operation of these rules or the provisions of any order, or by failure of any party to appear when required, may be restored (a) with the filed written consent of the parties or by order of a single appeal judge on application under rule 14.47 [Application to restore an appeal], and (b) on the payment of the fee for an application to restore an appeal in Schedule B.
(2) An order or written consent restoring an appeal must set deadlines and directions for the filing of any outstanding materials, and if the appellant fails to comply with any of those deadlines or directions, the appeal is deemed to have been struck again.
(3) An appeal or application is deemed to have been abandoned if no application to restore an appeal or application for permission to appeal has been filed, served and granted (a) for a standard appeal, within 6 months after having been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned, and (b) for a fast track appeal, within 3 months after having been struck, dismissed or deemed abandoned.

(a) remitting the matter back to the trial judge to decide the missing issue on the existing record ([rule] 14.75(1)(d));
(b) remitting the matter back for a new trial limited to that issue ([rules]
14.75(1)(d) and (f)), or (c) sending the entire cause of action back for a new trial ([rule] 14.75(1)(f)). Mikkelsen v. Truman Development Corp., [2017] A.J. No. 287, 2017 ABCA 99 at para. 36 (Alta. C.A.), citing , [2012] S.C.J. No. 44, 2012 SCC 44 at paras. 41-42 (S.C.C.).
